about.text: Steamed cheese is the Slovak way of turning matured sheep lump cheese into a plastic mass by working it in hot water, then pulling it into ribbons or strings. Parenica is wound into spirals, korbáčik braided; both are usually smoked and are traditionally sheep, now often cow.

picks.why: Poland's best-known smoked sheep cheese, a PDO from the Tatra Mountains, pressed in carved wooden moulds.
The defining Slovak steamed cheese, wound from strips into spirals, with PGI protection.
Slovakia's classic smoked steamed cheese, egg-shaped and decorated, protected as a PGI.
Braided string cheese of the Orava region, steamed and pulled into fine strands, shared by Slovakia and Poland.
The village-bound PGI form of korbáčik, made only in Žázrivá in northern Slovakia.
